key_insight: LongAgent frames longitudinal outcome prediction as a guided search problem, using history-aware agentic reasoning to identify the most predictive variables across messy, irregular medical timelines. The key idea is to turn heterogeneous patient histories into actionable predictions by focusing on informative past events rather than treating all measurements equally.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of predicting future clinical outcomes from longitudinal medical data that is heterogeneous, irregularly sampled, and spread across multiple sources. It tackles the challenge of extracting useful signals from many variables over time while filtering out noise, missingness, and irrelevant history.
method: Uses a history-guided agentic search strategy to examine longitudinal patient records over time.
Identifies variables and temporal patterns that are most predictive of future outcomes.
Integrates information across heterogeneous sources and irregular sampling intervals to build stronger outcome representations.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners in healthcare, this suggests a more interpretable and robust way to handle complex longitudinal data than flat aggregation or naive sequence modeling. It may improve prediction performance while also making it easier to understand which parts of a patient's history drive the model's decision.
visual_elements: A patient timeline showing irregular measurements from multiple sources
A flow diagram of history-guided agentic search selecting informative events
An attention-style highlight of predictive variables versus noisy variables
A before-and-after comparison of standard longitudinal modeling vs LongAgent
paper_title: LongAgent: History-Guided Agentic Search for Longitudinal Outcome Prediction
paper_authors: Siyao Wang, Florian Guitton, Shuojie Fu, Guanyu Tao, Kai Sun
